title: Ronnie Knows Beasts
description: Late-night pet advice on Snazzie FM. Worried owners call in about creatures they love. Ronnie answers every one with total confidence and zero competence, while Barry reads the voicemails and slowly loses his mind.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and it's the part of the night I live for. Ronnie Knows Beasts. You've got a pet, you've got a problem, I've got the answers.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, for the record, you have never owned an animal.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Which is exactly why I'm objective, Barry. Read me the first one.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay. This is Linda. She says her cat is older, and lately it's stopped eating, just sleeps by the radiator all day. She's scared something's wrong and she doesn't know whether to spend the money on the vet.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Oh, Linda, sweetheart, relax. A cat curled up by the warmth all day? That animal is living its best life.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: She said it stopped eating.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Intermittent fasting. Very trendy right now. Your cat's just ahead of the curve. <p:0.3> And listen, if you're really fretting about the vet bill... have you tried rehoming it?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Rehoming the... she loves that cat, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Then it'll understand. Next caller. Gary, you're on.

lines.speaker: caller-gary
lines.text: My dog destroys the place every time I leave. <p:0.3> Couch is gone. <p:0.3> Separation anxiety, probably.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Gary. Gary, stop. That's not anxiety. That dog is guarding your property. Like a professional.

lines.speaker: caller-gary
lines.text: He's... guarding it from me leaving?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: So you lean into it. Leave more. Stay gone longer. Really commit to the absence. Let that dog cook.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That is the opposite of every single thing a trainer would tell you.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And if it doesn't take, Gary? Rehome him. Win win. He gets a new couch, you get yours back.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That is not a win win, that's one win and a betrayal. Next one's a voicemail. Patricia.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Hello, um, my parrot has started screaming the same phrase, over and over, all day and all night. I'm worried he heard something upsetting, or maybe he's sick. I don't know where he even got it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Patricia. Patricia. Do you realize what you have? A talking bird is free advertising.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That is not the question she asked.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You teach him to say, Snazzie FM, ninety four point one. <p:0.3> See, that's a bird that contributes. Unlike some co-hosts, who never listen to a word I say.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I'm sorry, are we doing your feelings now? On the pet show?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: I listen to YOU, Barry. <p:0.3> Anyway. The puppy. Mildred, go.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh thank goodness. My new puppy eats everything off the floor, and just now I think, I think he swallowed a battery? A little round one? I'm panicking, what do I do, what's even safe?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Mildred. Breathe. Puppies have cast iron stomachs. Very robust little machines.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: It was a BATTERY though!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Which is just extra energy. That's literally where the word comes from. He'll be bouncing off the walls.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie. Ronnie, no. A battery is a vet emergency, that is genuinely dangerous, she needs to call a vet right now.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Barry, a little floor variety builds the immune system. You agree with me, you just won't say it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I... I do not... <p:0.3> it does sound a little robust, but no. No! Mildred, call a vet.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, he agreed. Last call of the night. Darnell, you're on Ronnie Knows Beasts.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Yeah, hey, so the kids' goldfish has been floating sideways at the top of the tank since this morning, and the kids keep asking me if he's gonna be okay, and I don't know what to tell them.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Darnell. Congratulations. That fish has learned to relax on its back. Like a little spa day.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: He's not moving, man.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Dim the lights. Bit of ambience. Let him have his moment. <p:0.3> And if he wants more? You know what I'm gonna say.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Do not say it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Rehome him.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Where, Ronnie? Where do you rehome a goldfish?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: The ocean, Barry. Set him free. Back to where he came from.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's a GOLDFISH! It's freshwater! It has never SEEN an ocean!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Then it'll be a lovely surprise for him, Barry.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's the show. That's the whole show. We have to take a break.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: One last voicemail came in while we were live. It's from Linda. <p:0.3> She says the cat's fine, the vet fixed it in twenty minutes, and she would like her question rehomed to a better show.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: <p:0.3> I'm inclined to agree, Linda.
